wa_ragged_edge.notes: Climb a layback flake into a low-angle groove to 3rd-class slabs, gear belay below a faint white dyke splitting the slab above (Blue Line variation, better rock than the original start).
Climb the dyke past three bolts to a thin ledge, then traverse right and up a short gully to the anchor.
Step right then traverse back left on positive edges toward the skyline; a single bolt and fixed pins protect a nice arête above.
Step right and climb steep, stacked blocks, then easy zig-zag cracks to the anchor; some semi-loose blocks warrant caution.
The crux pitch — step right and climb straight up in a very exposed position, taking gear well; at the second bolt, traverse right 50 ft to the anchor.
The "money pitch" — a long, easy romp up the exposed arête to the summit, capping the climb.

wa_sisu.notes: Start at the first line right of a 20 ft flake that forms a chimney against the wall; look for two bolts close together about 15 ft up. Knobs, tricky mantles and a little slab lead to Madsen's Ledge and a chain anchor. It is worth doing as a single pitch.

Walk about 20 ft right along the ledge and climb up a few boulders to reach the wall. The first bolt is well right of the line; backclean it if possible to cut drag. Traverse horizontal cracks, then crimp up and left to the belay.
Move horizontally right, underclinging the roof/flake system, until crimps appear above the lip of the roof and lead up to the belay.
Traverse left off the belay, then straight up into the first hard section. After a rest, follow the left-leaning crack system past several more difficult moves to a hanging belay.
A few tricky moves off the belay reach a large flake, then excellent edges lead up and right to a final hard section just below another hanging belay. Short but tied for the route's top grade.
Tenuous knobs and slopers give way to a fun flake system. Follow it to a knobby crux that moves right, then crimps and features lead up to a big ledge with a double-ring anchor.

About eight bolts. There are two belays: with a 60 m rope, stop at the anchor far left with huge chain links; to continue to the summit or rappel with a 70 m rope, carry on to a three-bolt anchor that includes a glue-in bolt.

wa_true_grit_2.notes: Easy climbing up clean granite to a bolted belay below an obvious narrow chimney; the exit move onto a short bolted slab above is the only real test on this pitch.
The squeeze chimney can be avoided by stepping right into a short corner instead; the traversing variation has some loose rock, so test holds carefully.
Slab moves lead into a shallow corner, then a pull over a small overhang on "jigsaw" rock to a cramped, exposed belay stance.

The route's namesake pitch and highlight — a long, sustained splitter finger-to-hand crack with a technical step-across where the crack briefly disappears; airy and exposed, considered one of the best moderate crack pitches in the area.
Short, scruffy finishing pitch of easy face and slab climbing to the top of the headwall; some topos mark this 5.8 but most parties find it closer to 5.6.
